```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(BreedReliabR)
```

## Purpose

BreedReliabR is a downstream decision-reliability package. It does not start from a raw yield spreadsheet, SNP file, or weather table. It starts after an upstream model has produced candidate environmental-response coefficient means and their full joint uncertainty covariance.

The workflow is:

```text
breeding data
  -> upstream prediction model
  -> candidate coefficient means + full joint covariance
  -> TPE
  -> BreedReliabR
  -> fixed-k advancement analysis
```

This vignette uses a small genotype-specific reaction-norm model fitted with base R only to make the hand-off transparent. It is not presented as a production genomic prediction model.

## 1. Simulate a small multi-environment trial

```{r data}
set.seed(2026)

n_gen <- 8
n_env <- 6
n_rep <- 2

genotypes <- paste0("G", sprintf("%02d", seq_len(n_gen)))
environments <- paste0("E", sprintf("%02d", seq_len(n_env)))

env <- data.frame(
  Environment = environments,
  Heat = c(24, 27, 29, 31, 33, 35),
  Water = c(72, 88, 60, 80, 55, 75)
)

heat_mean <- mean(env$Heat)
heat_sd <- sd(env$Heat)
water_mean <- mean(env$Water)
water_sd <- sd(env$Water)

env$heat_z <- (env$Heat - heat_mean) / heat_sd
env$water_z <- (env$Water - water_mean) / water_sd
env$intercept <- 1

basis_names <- c("intercept", "heat_z", "water_z")
training_basis <- as.matrix(env[, basis_names])
rownames(training_basis) <- env$Environment
```

The training transformation is now frozen. A real analysis must apply the same transformation to target environments rather than standardising the TPE separately.

## 2. Generate synthetic phenotype observations

```{r phenotype}
true_coef <- cbind(
  intercept = rnorm(n_gen, 5.0, 0.30),
  heat_z = rnorm(n_gen, -0.25, 0.12),
  water_z = rnorm(n_gen, 0.25, 0.12)
)
rownames(true_coef) <- genotypes

dat <- expand.grid(
  Genotype = genotypes,
  Environment = environments,
  Rep = seq_len(n_rep),
  KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

dat <- merge(dat, env, by = "Environment", sort = FALSE)
dat <- dat[
  order(match(dat$Genotype, genotypes),
        match(dat$Environment, environments),
        dat$Rep),
]
rownames(dat) <- NULL

g_index <- match(dat$Genotype, genotypes)
dat$Yield <-
  true_coef[g_index, "intercept"] +
  true_coef[g_index, "heat_z"] * dat$heat_z +
  true_coef[g_index, "water_z"] * dat$water_z +
  rnorm(nrow(dat), 0, 0.25)

head(dat[, c("Genotype", "Environment", "Rep", "Yield")])
```

At this point the data are still ordinary multi-environment trial observations. BreedReliabR has not yet been used.

## 3. Fit a transparent reaction-norm model outside BreedReliabR

Each genotype receives an intercept, heat-response coefficient, and water-response coefficient.

```{r fit}
p <- length(basis_names)

X <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(dat), ncol = n_gen * p)
for (i in seq_along(genotypes)) {
  rows <- dat$Genotype == genotypes[i]
  cols <- ((i - 1) * p + 1):(i * p)
  X[rows, cols] <- as.matrix(dat[rows, basis_names])
}

coefficient_order <- unlist(
  lapply(genotypes, function(g) paste(g, basis_names, sep = "__")),
  use.names = FALSE
)
colnames(X) <- coefficient_order

fit <- lm.fit(X, dat$Yield)
stopifnot(fit$rank == ncol(X))

beta_hat <- fit$coefficients
coef_mean <- matrix(
  beta_hat,
  nrow = n_gen,
  ncol = p,
  byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(genotypes, basis_names)
)

sigma2 <- sum(fit$residuals^2) / fit$df.residual
coef_vcov <- sigma2 * solve(crossprod(X))
rownames(coef_vcov) <- coefficient_order
colnames(coef_vcov) <- coefficient_order

dim(coef_mean)
dim(coef_vcov)
```

For eight candidates and three coefficients, BreedReliabR receives an 8 x 3 mean matrix and a 24 x 24 joint covariance.

In this pedagogical fixed-effect model, `coef_vcov` is the joint coefficient-estimation covariance. It demonstrates the required matrix structure; it is not a genomic prediction-error covariance and should not be substituted for the PEV from a properly fitted genomic model.

## 4. Verify ordering and covariance structure

```{r checks}
expected_order <- unlist(
  lapply(genotypes, function(g) paste(g, basis_names, sep = "__")),
  use.names = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  identical(rownames(coef_vcov), expected_order),
  identical(colnames(coef_vcov), expected_order),
  all(is.finite(coef_mean)),
  all(is.finite(coef_vcov)),
  isSymmetric(coef_vcov, tol = 1e-8)
)

pev_eigen <- eigen(coef_vcov, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
pev_scale <- max(1, max(abs(pev_eigen)))
stopifnot(min(pev_eigen) >= -1e-8 * pev_scale)
```

Candidate-major ordering means all basis coefficients for candidate 1, then all coefficients for candidate 2, and so on. Correct dimensions alone cannot prove correct ordering.

## 5. Specify the target population of environments

```{r target}
tpe_raw <- data.frame(
  State = paste0("TPE", 1:4),
  Heat = c(26, 30, 33, 35),
  Water = c(82, 72, 63, 56),
  Weight = c(0.20, 0.30, 0.30, 0.20)
)

tpe_raw$heat_z <- (tpe_raw$Heat - heat_mean) / heat_sd
tpe_raw$water_z <- (tpe_raw$Water - water_mean) / water_sd
tpe_raw$intercept <- 1

tpe_basis <- as.matrix(tpe_raw[, basis_names])
rownames(tpe_basis) <- tpe_raw$State
tpe_weights <- tpe_raw$Weight
```

The weights are assumptions describing the target distribution over the supplied states. They are not automatically acreage or production-area weights.

## 6. Preflight the hand-off

```{r preflight}
input_check <- br_check_inputs(
  candidates = genotypes,
  coef_mean = coef_mean,
  coef_vcov = coef_vcov,
  basis_names = basis_names,
  tpe_basis = tpe_basis,
  tpe_weights = tpe_weights,
  training_basis = training_basis,
  k = 3,
  H = 5
)
input_check
```

A PASS establishes structural compatibility only. It does not validate the upstream model, covariance adequacy, biological definition of the TPE, or empirical probability calibration.

## 7. BreedReliabR begins here

```{r objects}
prediction <- br_prediction(
  candidates = genotypes,
  coef_mean = coef_mean,
  coef_vcov = coef_vcov,
  basis_names = basis_names,
  source = "Pedagogical genotype-specific reaction-norm model"
)

tpe <- br_tpe(
  basis = tpe_basis,
  weights = tpe_weights,
  state_id = tpe_raw$State
)

prediction
tpe
```

## 8. Diagnose geometric support

```{r support}
support <- br_support(tpe, training_basis)
support
plot(support)
```

`br_support()` is a geometric extrapolation diagnostic. It does not prove biological validity, prediction accuracy, or calibration.

## 9. Compare environmental and prediction uncertainty

```{r omega}
omega <- br_omega(prediction, tpe, H = c(1, 3, 5, 10))
omega$summary
head(omega$candidate)
```

Omega is the ratio of finite-TPE environmental variance to prediction variance. It is not a probability, selection gain, genetic gain, or universal threshold.

## 10. Compare M0-M3 and estimate advancement probabilities

```{r advancement}
comparison <- br_compare(
  prediction, tpe, H = 5, k = 3,
  nsim = 1000, seed = 2026
)
summary(comparison)

advancement <- br_advance(
  prediction, tpe, H = 5, k = 3,
  nsim = 2000, method = "M3", seed = 2026
)
advancement$candidates
sum(advancement$candidates$p_advance)
```

M0 is deterministic point ranking. M1 propagates prediction uncertainty, M2 finite-TPE uncertainty, and M3 both. These are uncertainty formulations of the same prediction object, not different genomic models.

For M1-M3, `p_advance` is a conditional top-k inclusion probability. Selected-set reliability is an expected retained fraction, not the probability of recovering the complete set.

## 11. Examine sensitivity to H

```{r curve}
curve_results <- br_curve(
  prediction, tpe,
  H = c(1, 3, 5, 10),
  k = 3,
  nsim = 1000,
  seed = 2026
)
summary(curve_results)
plot(curve_results, type = "reliability")
plot(curve_results, type = "omega")
```

`H` is the number of independent future draws from the specified TPE whose average represents the future environmental target under the current formulation. It is not the number of training environments, and BreedReliabR does not automatically identify an optimal H.

## 12. Export the operational hand-off

```{r export}
template_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "BreedReliabR_beginner_example")
dir.create(template_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

candidate_coefficients <- data.frame(
  candidate = rownames(coef_mean),
  coef_mean,
  check.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  candidate_coefficients,
  file.path(template_dir, "candidate_coefficients.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

saveRDS(
  coef_vcov,
  file.path(template_dir, "candidate_joint_PEV.rds")
)

write.csv(
  data.frame(
    state = tpe_raw$State,
    tpe_basis,
    weight = tpe_weights,
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  file.path(template_dir, "target_environments.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  data.frame(
    environment = rownames(training_basis),
    training_basis,
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  file.path(template_dir, "training_environments.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

These four files illustrate the operational boundary between an upstream model-fitting workflow and BreedReliabR.

## 13. Common mistakes

Do not supply raw SNP or phenotype tables directly to `br_prediction()`. Do not replace the full joint covariance with marginal standard errors. Do not fit a separate standardisation or PCA to target environments. Do not interpret H as training size, Omega as selection gain, or selected-set reliability as exact-set recovery probability.

Increasing `nsim` reduces Monte Carlo error only; it cannot correct an inadequate upstream predictive distribution or poorly specified TPE.
